title: The Bundle of Sticks: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: The oldest son broke the sticks that were tied together.
The other boys pulled and bent the sticks, but the sticks did not break.
The boys could not break one stick.
At the end, the boys argued more.
What did the father do with the sticks first?
options: He put them in the fire

items.q: Who tried to break the sticks first?
items.why: “He gave the sticks to his oldest son.”

items.q: What did the father give each boy after he untied the sticks?
What did the boys say when they broke one stick?
What did the father say the sticks are like?
items.why: "These sticks are like you," he said.

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: A father had three sons who argued every day. He showed them that they could not break the sticks when they were tied together, but they could easily break one stick. He told them that together they are strong, and the boys stopped arguing.

items.q: Why did the father tie the sticks together?
items.model: He wanted to help his sons, because they argued every day.

items.q: What happened when the father untied the sticks?
items.model: He gave each boy one stick, and each boy broke his stick easily.

items.q: What did the father want his sons to understand?
items.model: Together, they are strong. They should help each other every day.

items.q: When do you work together with your friends or family?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: The father tied some sticks together
The oldest son tried to break the sticks
The other boys pulled and bent the sticks
